front: Hormones of the islets of Langerhans
back: Alpha cells: glucagon (raises glucose). Beta cells: insulin (lowers glucose).
More GLUT4 in muscle and fat cell membranes; glycogenesis; more respiration of glucose; glucose to fat.
On liver cells: glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; glucose released into blood.
Receptor → G-protein → adenylyl cyclase → ATP to cAMP → protein kinase A → cascade → glycogen phosphorylase.
Molecule (e.g. cAMP) inside a cell that relays the signal from a hormone bound to a surface receptor.
Making glucose from non-carbohydrates (amino acids, glycerol) in the liver.

front: Enzymes on urine glucose test strips
back: Glucose oxidase (glucose → H₂O₂) and peroxidase (H₂O₂ + chromogen → colour).
Each activated enzyme activates many of the next, so a little hormone gives a large, fast response.
